quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #8
										  					
  

30 Questions • Passing Score 21

questions.question: What causes "highway hypnosis"?

options.text: Staring at the road for a long time.
Taking frequent rest stops.
Getting too much sleep the night before.
Driving short distances on expressways.

questions.correctAnswerText: Staring at the road for a long time.
questions.explanation: Highway hypnosis happens when you stare straight ahead without looking around. You stop watching traffic and your surroundings. This makes you likely to crash into vehicles slowing down or stopping in front of you.

questions.question: Your vehicle is blocking traffic after an accident. What should you do?

options.text: Move your vehicle off the road if you can.
Do not move your vehicle under any circumstances.
Wait for police before moving your vehicle.
None of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move your vehicle off the road if you can.
questions.explanation: After a minor accident, move your vehicle off the road if possible. Always stay at the accident scene. Tell the other driver who you are and offer help if needed.

questions.question: How can you avoid carbon monoxide poisoning while driving?

options.text: Have your exhaust system checked regularly for leaks.
Keep your car off when parked in a closed garage.
Close your vents when driving close behind another car.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Carbon monoxide is a deadly gas you cannot see or smell. Poisoning causes tiredness, yawning, dizziness, and nausea. Fresh air is the only cure.

questions.question: What lights should you use when driving in fog?

options.text: Low beam headlights.
High beam headlights.
Parking lights.
Hazard flashers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Low beam headlights.
questions.explanation: In fog, use low beam headlights and fog lights if you have them. High beams point upward and bounce off fog back into your eyes, making it harder to see.

questions.question: What affects your ability to stop?

options.text: Signal lights.
Other cars on the road.
The time of day.
The condition of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: The condition of the road.
questions.explanation: Road conditions greatly affect your stopping ability. Drive slower on poor roads. Slippery roads make it dangerous to stop quickly.

questions.question: Two vehicles reach an intersection at the same time with no signs or signals. Who has the right-of-way?

options.text: The car coming from the right.
The car coming from the left.
The car that honks first.
The car traveling fastest.

questions.correctAnswerText: The car coming from the right.
questions.explanation: At an intersection with no traffic signs or signals, you must yield to a vehicle coming from your right.

questions.question: Your wheels slip off the edge of the road. What should you do?

options.text: Jerk the steering wheel to force the vehicle back onto the road.
Speed up and steer back onto the road gradually.
Slam on the brakes and stop.
Slow down gently with the brakes. Then turn the wheel slowly to return to the road at a safe speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down gently with the brakes. Then turn the wheel slowly to return to the road at a safe speed.
questions.explanation: If your wheels leave the road, keep driving on the shoulder. Gently use the brakes to slow down. When you are at a safe speed, slowly turn the wheel to get back onto the road. Do not jerk the wheel sharply.

questions.question: What is the most common cause of traffic crashes?

options.text: New drivers
Human error
Bad weather
Bad roads

questions.correctAnswerText: Human error
questions.explanation: Crashes often happen when drivers do not see other vehicles or do something unexpected. Communicate with other drivers to help prevent crashes.

questions.question: You see a sign that says "Reduced speed, 35 mph." What does this mean?

options.text: The new 35 mph speed limit starts at this sign.
The new 35 mph speed limit starts at the next speed limit sign.
You have plenty of time to slow down before the reduced speed zone.
Reduce your speed to 35 mph only in bad weather.

questions.correctAnswerText: The new 35 mph speed limit starts at this sign.
questions.explanation: Reduced speed signs tell you to lower your speed. The new speed limit begins at the sign where you see it.

questions.question: Which statement about winter driving is false?

options.text: Winter is the hardest season to drive in.
Check your antifreeze and windshield washer fluid in winter.
Using cruise control in winter weather is safe.
Snow tires are a good choice for winter driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Using cruise control in winter weather is safe.
questions.explanation: Do not use cruise control on snow, rain, fog, or similar dangerous conditions. Winter driving is hard and requires extra care. Check your antifreeze and windshield washer fluid. Snow tires help your vehicle grip slippery roads.

questions.question: A stop sign is shaped like a(n):

options.text: Rectangle.
Square.
Circle.
Octagon.

questions.correctAnswerText: Octagon.
questions.explanation: Only stop signs are octagonal (eight-sided). This shape tells drivers to stop completely before moving forward.

questions.question: When is it illegal to drive below the speed limit?

options.text: When driving slowly disrupts the normal flow of traffic
When in heavy traffic in a construction zone
Only when driving in rural areas.
When driving under adverse weather conditions

questions.correctAnswerText: When driving slowly disrupts the normal flow of traffic
questions.explanation: Driving too slowly can disrupt traffic and is illegal. You may be cited for driving slower than traffic conditions allow.

questions.question: After stopping for a school bus that is unloading children:

options.text: Do not proceed until the children wave to you.
Watch for children walking along the side of the road.
Accelerate quickly.
Turn on your emergency flashers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Watch for children walking along the side of the road.
questions.explanation: After the school bus stops and unloads children, watch carefully for children walking near the road. Always drive slowly and carefully near children.

questions.question: Do not pass:

options.text: On a hill or curve.
When school bus lights are flashing.
When approaching an intersection.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Never pass on hills or curves where you cannot see ahead, at intersections, at railroad crossings, on bridges, or when a school bus has flashing red lights. Do not pass in any no-passing zone.

questions.question: When you hear the siren or see the flashing lights of an approaching emergency vehicle, you must:

options.text: Slow down until it passes you.
Drive to the right side of the road and stop.
Motion for the emergency vehicle to pass you.
Merge into the right lane and continue driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive to the right side of the road and stop.
questions.explanation: Always yield to emergency vehicles using sirens or flashing lights. Move to the right side of the road and stop. If you are in an intersection, drive through it first, then stop on the right side.

questions.question: If you become stranded in a snowstorm, the best thing to do is to:

options.text: Get out of the car and go for help.
Lay down in your car and go to sleep.
Walk into the road and get the attention of other drivers.
Stay in the car, as you are most likely to be found when you stay in your vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay in the car, as you are most likely to be found when you stay in your vehicle.
questions.explanation: Stay in your car if stranded in a snowstorm. Rescuers will find you more easily if you remain in your vehicle. Walking around in a snowstorm is dangerous.

questions.question: From the center lane, which maneuver(s) can you perform?

options.text: You may make left turns.
You may make U-turns.
You may pass slow-moving traffic.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may make left turns.
questions.explanation: A center turn lane is for left turns only. You cannot use it for passing or driving straight through.

questions.question: Which offense will cause a license to be automatically suspended?

options.text: Racing while on a public roadway
Graffiti
Lending a license to another individual
All of the above

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above
questions.explanation: Your license is automatically suspended if you are convicted of racing on a public road, committing graffiti, or lending your license to someone else.

questions.question: This road sign means:

options.text: Hunting area.
State park.
Deer crossing.
Wildlife preserve.

questions.correctAnswerText: Deer crossing.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that deer cross the road in this area. Slow down and be ready to stop.

questions.question: At dusk or on overcast days, you should:

options.text: Drive using your four-way flashers.
Drive using your parking lights.
Not turn on any vehicle lights.
Turn on your headlights.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn on your headlights.
questions.explanation: Turn on your headlights at dusk and on overcast days. Use low beams when within 1,000 feet of oncoming cars or 500 feet behind another car. Always use low beams in poor weather.

questions.question: You may drive in the HOV lane if:

options.text: Your vehicle has two or more people in it.
You are driving slower than other traffic.
You are driving faster than other traffic.
You are trying to get somewhere quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Your vehicle has two or more people in it.
questions.explanation: Some highways have a left lane only for vehicles with two or more people. These are called HOV (High Occupancy Vehicle) lanes. Signs and diamond symbols on the road mark these lanes.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: Low clearance.
Fines double in a work zone.
No left turn.
Do not block intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: Low clearance.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are usually yellow with black markings. They tell drivers about road conditions and dangers ahead. This sign warns you that the road ahead has low clearance.

questions.question: This road sign means:

options.text: Drive with caution and be ready to slow down.
Do not drive in this lane.
You must stop completely and yield the right-of-way.
Slow down, be ready to stop, and yield the right-of-way if needed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down, be ready to stop, and yield the right-of-way if needed.
questions.explanation: This triangular sign means you must yield. Slow down as you approach the intersection and be ready to stop. Let other vehicles, cyclists, and pedestrians pass safely before you go.

questions.question: How can you lower the risk of hydroplaning?

options.text: Do not speed when roads are wet.
Use tires with the correct air pressure.
Replace tires that have worn tread.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Hydroplaning happens when your vehicle slides on a thin layer of water between the tires and road. Tires with low air pressure or worn tread increase this risk. Speeding also increases the risk.

questions.question: When in a travel lane on the roadway:

options.text: You may stop to drop off passengers.
You may stop to look up an address.
You may make a U-turn or back up if you miss a freeway entrance ramp.
Do not stop for any reason. Keep moving until you can safely pull off the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not stop for any reason. Keep moving until you can safely pull off the road.
questions.explanation: Never stop in a travel lane. Keep moving until you can safely pull off the road. If you miss your turn or exit, do not back up. Continue to the next turn or exit where you can safely turn around.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: Trucks under 18,000 lbs. allowed.
Hill ahead.
Truck stop ahead.
No trucks allowed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hill ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that a steep hill is coming up ahead.

questions.question: On a two-lane street, a fire engine is following your vehicle without flashing lights or sirens. You should:

options.text: Continue to drive normally.
Stop as quickly as you can.
Speed up to get out of its way.
Slow down, move to the right, and stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Continue to drive normally.
questions.explanation: If an emergency vehicle is behind you without a siren or flashing lights, you do not need to move. Drive normally.

questions.question: Which traffic light tells you to slow down and proceed with caution at an intersection?

options.text: A flashing yellow light
A flashing red light
A solid yellow light
A solid red light

questions.correctAnswerText: A flashing yellow light
questions.explanation: A flashing yellow light means slow down, proceed with caution, and be ready to stop.

questions.question: To use a roundabout correctly, drivers should:

options.text: Stop within the roundabout.
Yield to traffic entering the roundabout.
Drive in a clockwise direction.
Yield to traffic already in the roundabout.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yield to traffic already in the roundabout.
questions.explanation: A roundabout is a circular intersection with no traffic light. Traffic flows counterclockwise around a central island. Enter from the right and yield to cars already in the roundabout. Follow the circle until you reach your exit.

questions.question: You are driving on a narrow road when you meet an oncoming vehicle. You must:

options.text: Pull completely off the road and stop.
Give the oncoming vehicle at least half of the road.
Demand the other vehicle pull over.
Turn on your high beam headlights so they can see you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Give the oncoming vehicle at least half of the road.
questions.explanation: On narrow roads, you must give vehicles coming toward you at least half of the road space. Both vehicles need enough space to pass each other safely.
